title: T13 Liquidation, Funding and Futures Risks

lines.text: Lesson thirteen: liquidation, funding and futures risks. What can close a position for you.
lines.say: Lesson thirteen: liquidation, funding and futures risks. What can close a position for you.

lines.text: Imagine you open a 10x long. Then BTC falls, and you see this.
lines.say: Imagine you open a ten ex long. Then B-T-C falls, and you see this.

lines.text: Your position was closed by the exchange. You didn't press anything.
lines.say: Your position was closed by the exchange. You didn't press anything.

lines.text: That's called liquidation. Let's see how it happens, step by step.
lines.say: That's called liquidation. Let's see how it happens, step by step.

lines.text: Start with your margin balance: your margin plus the open profit or loss.
lines.say: Start with your margin balance: your margin plus the open profit or loss.

lines.text: A 10x long: 100 USDT of margin, 1,000 USDT notional, entry 60,000.
lines.say: A ten ex long: one hundred U-S-D-T of margin, one thousand U-S-D-T notional, entry sixty thousand.

lines.text: BTC falls 1%: 90 left. Falls 3%: 70 left. Falls 5%: only 50 left.
lines.say: B-T-C falls one percent: ninety left. Falls three percent: seventy left. Falls five percent: only fifty left.

lines.text: Each fall eats into the room left above the maintenance level.
lines.say: Each fall eats into the room left above the maintenance level.

lines.text: Liquidation is a forced closure. The exchange closes your position for you.
lines.say: Liquidation is a forced closure. The exchange closes your position for you.

lines.text: It happens when your margin balance falls to the maintenance level.
lines.say: It happens when your margin balance falls to the maintenance level.

lines.text: You don't choose the price or the moment. Most or all of the margin can be gone.
lines.say: You don't choose the price or the moment. Most or all of the margin can be gone.

lines.text: Like a rental firm taking the car back early. Each exchange has its own rules.
lines.say: Like a rental firm taking the car back early. Each exchange has its own rules.

lines.text: Leverage changes how much room you have.
lines.say: Leverage changes how much room you have.

lines.text: Same 1,000 USDT position. At 10x you put in 100. At 4x, 250.
lines.say: Same one thousand U-S-D-T position. At ten ex you put in one hundred. At four ex, two hundred fifty.

lines.text: A 5% fall costs 50 USDT either way. At 10x, half your margin is gone. At 4x, a fifth.
lines.say: A five percent fall costs fifty U-S-D-T either way. At ten ex, half your margin is gone. At four ex, a fifth.

lines.text: More room is not safety. A big enough move can reach any level.
lines.say: More room is not safety. A big enough move can reach any level.

lines.text: Exchanges usually check liquidation against the mark price, not only the last trade.
lines.say: Exchanges usually check liquidation against the mark price, not only the last trade.

lines.text: The mark price is a reference price the exchange works out, often from several markets.
lines.say: The mark price is a reference price the exchange works out, often from several markets.

lines.text: Here one odd trade spikes down. The last price jumps. The mark price moves much less.
lines.say: Here one odd trade spikes down. The last price jumps. The mark price moves much less.

lines.text: But in a real crash, it falls too.
lines.say: But in a real crash, it falls too.

lines.text: Now funding. Perpetual futures never expire, so they need a way to stay near the spot price.
lines.say: Now funding. Perpetual futures never expire, so they need a way to stay near the spot price.

lines.text: The funding rate sets a payment between longs and shorts, at set times, often every 8 hours.
lines.say: The funding rate sets a payment between longs and shorts, at set times, often every eight hours.

lines.text: Positive rate: longs pay shorts. Negative rate: shorts pay longs.
lines.say: Positive rate: longs pay shorts. Negative rate: shorts pay longs.

lines.text: Example: 1,000 USDT times 0.01% is 0.10 USDT each time.
lines.say: Example: one thousand U-S-D-T times zero point zero one percent is zero point one U-S-D-T each time.

lines.text: Funding adds up when you hold a position for a long time.
lines.say: Funding adds up when you hold a position for a long time.

lines.text: Three times a day for three days is nine payments: 0.90 USDT at 1,000 notional.
lines.say: Three times a day for three days is nine payments: zero point nine U-S-D-T at one thousand notional.

lines.text: At 10,000 notional, 9 USDT. Real rates change, and can be much higher.
lines.say: At ten thousand notional, nine U-S-D-T. Real rates change, and can be much higher.

lines.text: Funding comes out of your margin balance too.
lines.say: Funding comes out of your margin balance too.

lines.text: Gap risk. Sometimes price jumps from one level to another, with no trades in between.
lines.say: Gap risk. Sometimes price jumps from one level to another, with no trades in between.

lines.text: Your stop-loss is at 59,000. News hits. Price jumps from 59,600 straight to 58,300.
lines.say: Your stop-loss is at fifty-nine thousand. News hits. Price jumps from fifty-nine thousand six hundred straight to fifty-eight thousand three hundred.

lines.text: The stop triggers, but it fills near 58,300. A bigger loss than planned.
lines.say: The stop triggers, but it fills near fifty-eight thousand three hundred. A bigger loss than planned.

lines.text: A gap can bring liquidation just as suddenly.
lines.say: A gap can bring liquidation just as suddenly.

lines.text: A common mistake: thinking a stop-loss protects you from liquidation.
lines.say: A common mistake: thinking a stop-loss protects you from liquidation.

lines.text: With high leverage, the liquidation zone can sit closer than your stop.
lines.say: With high leverage, the liquidation zone can sit closer than your stop.

lines.text: Then the position is liquidated before the stop is ever reached.
lines.say: Then the position is liquidated before the stop is ever reached.

lines.text: And in a gap, a stop can fill late. A stop-loss is not liquidation insurance.
lines.say: And in a gap, a stop can fill late. A stop-loss is not liquidation insurance.

lines.text: Your turn. BTC is swinging hard before big news. Your buffer is small. You're unsure.
lines.say: Your turn. B-T-C is swinging hard before big news. Your buffer is small. You're unsure.

lines.text: What's the sensible choice: A, B or C? Pause if you need more time.
lines.say: What's the sensible choice: A, B or C? Pause if you need more time.

lines.text: C. Reduce your exposure or close, then wait. No trade is a real decision.
lines.say: C. Reduce your exposure or close, then wait. No trade is a real decision.

lines.text: Adding leverage to win it back makes the next move hit harder.
lines.say: Adding leverage to win it back makes the next move hit harder.

lines.text: Before you go further, know the risks of futures.
lines.say: Before you go further, know the risks of futures.

lines.text: Liquidation can take most or all of your margin, at a price you didn't choose.
lines.say: Liquidation can take most or all of your margin, at a price you didn't choose.

lines.text: Funding is paid or charged every period, and the rate keeps changing.
lines.say: Funding is paid or charged every period, and the rate keeps changing.

lines.text: Gaps and slippage can make exits worse than planned.
lines.say: Gaps and slippage can make exits worse than planned.

lines.text: No strategy is guaranteed safe. When unsure, reduce exposure or choose no trade.
lines.say: No strategy is guaranteed safe. When unsure, reduce exposure or choose no trade.

lines.text: Let's recap.
lines.say: Let's recap.

lines.text: Liquidation is a forced closure when your margin balance hits the maintenance level.
lines.say: Liquidation is a forced closure when your margin balance hits the maintenance level.

lines.text: Funding is a regular payment between longs and shorts on perpetual futures.
lines.say: Funding is a regular payment between longs and shorts on perpetual futures.

lines.text: A stop-loss is not liquidation insurance. Waiting is always allowed.
lines.say: A stop-loss is not liquidation insurance. Waiting is always allowed.

lines.text: Check yourself: can a stop-loss guarantee you won't be liquidated?
lines.say: Check yourself: can a stop-loss guarantee you won't be liquidated?

lines.text: No. Stops can slip, and liquidation can come first.
lines.say: No. Stops can slip, and liquidation can come first.

lines.text: Phase 3 complete! Next up: Checkpoint A, a review of lessons T01 to T13.
lines.say: Phase three complete! Next up: Checkpoint A, a review of lessons T one to T thirteen.
